title: Alert noise review — Private Observability Minimum Pack (v1)
content:
Context / intent
- This sheet is a noise-focused pass over the proposed Prometheus alert rules shipping with the “Private observability minimum pack”.
- Goal: ship a default set of alerts that are actionable in customer clusters, with bounded cardinality and reasonable thresholds across VPC + on-prem footprints.
- This is NOT the “premium” alert set; we prioritize high-signal failure modes and SLO burn.

Assumptions used for expected noise
- Private installs vary widely; thresholds below assume:
  - 2–20 inference runtime pods, 1–4 control plane replicas per service.
  - 5–500 RPS equivalent (tokenized workloads vary; use request-based signals where possible).
  - Prometheus scrape interval: 30s; evaluation interval: 30s.
  - Customer may have aggressive NetworkPolicies; scrape failures are common post-change.
- “Expected noise” ratings are based on (a) staging private cluster burn-in, (b) Support tickets, (c) SRE prior incident patterns.

Severity + paging policy (Private)
- Sev0 (Page): Customer-facing outage / widespread request failures or sustained hard SLO burn with no capacity headroom.
- Sev1 (Page): High likelihood of imminent outage (e.g., crash loop across runtime pool, GPU OOM storm), or rapid burn (short window).
- Sev2 (Ticket): Degradation / early warning requiring follow-up but not immediate response.
- Sev3 (Info): For dashboards / reporting only (avoid shipping as alerts by default).

Default behavior in the minimum pack
- “Enabled by default” means: rule ships enabled in the Helm chart values for the minimum pack.
- We will ship additional rules as “available but disabled” where they tend to be customer-environment-specific.

Table legend
- Noise risk: Low / Med / High
- Suggested action: Page / Ticket / Dashboard-only
- Notes include tuning guidance and common false positives.

Proposed alerts review (v1)
| ID | Alert name | Area | Signal | Proposed expr (summary) | Threshold / for | Suggested Sev | Suggested action | Enabled by default | Noise risk | Expected false positives / notes | Runbook anchor |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | RedwoodAPIAvailabilityBurn | API gateway | SLO burn (availability) | multiwindow burn on 5xx + timeouts | 2% error budget; fast(5m/1h) + slow(30m/6h) | Sev0 | Page | Yes | Low | Needs clear definition of “5xx” across gateway + upstream. Confirm excludes client cancels. Ensure alert annotation includes cluster + namespace. | private-day2:api-availability |
| A2 | RedwoodAPILatencyBurnP95 | API gateway | SLO burn (latency) | multiwindow burn on p95 latency | p95 > SLO; fast + slow windows | Sev1 | Page | Yes | Med | Latency SLO differs by customer route/model. Use route_class (coarse) not route_id. If customer pins to very large context models, expect chronic burn; provide tuning doc. | private-day2:latency-burn |
| A3 | RedwoodAPILatencyBurnP99 | API gateway | SLO burn (tail) | multiwindow burn on p99 | p99 > SLO | Sev1 | Ticket (unless fast burn) | Yes (Sev1), but route-scoped annotations | Med | P99 is spiky at low volume; gate on req rate > min (e.g., > 1 rps) or use “AND request_count > N”. Consider default: ticket unless fast burn is > 14.4x. | private-day2:latency-burn |
| A4 | RedwoodHigh5xxRate | API gateway | Error rate | 5xx ratio over 5m | >2% for 10m | Sev1 | Page | Yes | Med | Often trips during customer deploys/rollouts if not suppressed. Add recommendation: silence during planned upgrades. Should ignore 499/408 if possible. | private-day2:error-rate |
| A5 | RedwoodElevated4xxRate | API gateway | Client error | 4xx ratio | >20% for 15m | Sev3 | Dashboard-only | No | High | Mostly customer misconfig/auth; not actionable for Redwood on-call. Keep as panel. If shipped as alert, do ticket to customer platform team. | private-day2:auth-errors |
| R1 | RuntimeRequestQueueDepthHigh | runtime | Saturation/backpressure | queue_depth gauge | > (pods * 200) for 10m | Sev1 | Page | Yes | Med | Queue behavior differs by batching config. Use recording rules to normalize per-pod. False positives during traffic spikes if autoscaling disabled. Add “AND GPU util > 80%” if available. | private-day2:queueing |
| R2 | RuntimeBatchingDisabledUnexpected | runtime | Perf regression | batching_enabled == 0 | 0 for 15m | Sev2 | Ticket | No (ship disabled) | High | Some customers disable batching intentionally. Keep as disabled-by-default with doc note. | private-day2:batching |
| R3 | RuntimeTokenThroughputDrop | runtime | Throughput | tokens/sec vs baseline | <50% of 1h median for 15m | Sev2 | Ticket | No | High | Baseline is hard in Private (workload shifts). Not suitable for v1 default alerts. Prefer dashboard + SRE guide for optional enablement. | private-day2:throughput |
| R4 | RuntimeHighErrorRate | runtime | Serving errors | error ratio | >1% for 10m | Sev1 | Page | Yes | Low | Use coarse error_code groups to avoid cardinality. Ensure includes model load failures separately. | private-day2:runtime-errors |
| R5 | RuntimePodCrashLooping | runtime | Restarts | restarts > X | >3 restarts/10m (per pod) | Sev1 | Page | Yes | Low | High-signal. Include pod name + node. If all pods restart simultaneously, likely bad rollout or config. | private-day2:crashloop |
| R6 | RuntimeOOMKilled | runtime | OOM | OOMKilled count | >=1 OOM kill/10m (per deployment) | Sev1 | Page | Yes | Med | Some single OOMs happen on first load (model warmup). Add “for: 5m” and require >=2 events within window, OR “increase memory” runbook. | private-day2:oom |
| R7 | GPUUtilizationSustainedHigh | runtime | GPU saturation | avg GPU util | >95% for 20m | Sev2 | Ticket | Yes | Med | High GPU util is often normal; actionable only when paired with latency burn/queue growth. Recommend: ticket by default; customers can promote to page. Add cross-signal note in annotations. | private-day2:gpu-saturation |
| R8 | GPUMemoryUtilizationHigh | runtime | GPU mem pressure | GPU mem used ratio | >95% for 15m | Sev2 | Ticket | Yes | Med | Similar to R7. Actionable when OOMs occur. Keep as ticket-level. | private-day2:gpu-mem |
| R9 | NodeGPUExporterDown | infra | Observability dependency | scrape target down | >10m | Sev2 | Ticket | Yes | Med | Common with NetworkPolicies + DaemonSet scheduling constraints. Not page-worthy unless tied to inability to manage SLOs. | private-day2:scrape-failures |
| O1 | PrometheusTargetDownRedwoodServices | observability | Scrape | up==0 for Redwood jobs | >10m | Sev2 | Ticket | Yes | Med | Common after NP changes (see incident thread). Provide “first check: networkpolicy + serviceMonitor selectors + TLS”. | private-day2:scrape-failures |
| O2 | PrometheusTSDBDiskFilling | observability | Storage pressure | disk usage / WAL growth | >80% for 30m | Sev1 | Page | Yes | Low | Very actionable (Prometheus dies, lose signals). Include remediation: expand PVC / reduce retention / remote write. | private-day2:prom-storage |
| O3 | PrometheusRemoteWriteBackpressure | observability | Export pipeline | remote write queue | >0.8 capacity for 15m | Sev2 | Ticket | No (ship disabled) | High | Not all customers enable remote_write. False positives if sink rate-limits. Keep disabled by default; provide as optional for SIEM export setups. | private-day2:remote-write |
| C1 | ControlPlaneServiceDown | control plane | Availability | deployment replicas unavailable | any cp deployment unavailable for 10m | Sev1 | Page | Yes | Low | Page-worthy if impacts routing/auth/config. Add service name to alert. | private-day2:control-plane |
| C2 | ControlPlaneHigh5xx | control plane | Error rate | 5xx ratio | >2% for 10m | Sev2 | Ticket | Yes | Med | Often secondary to gateway errors; use as supporting signal. Page only if correlated with A1/A4. | private-day2:control-plane |
| M1 | ModelRegistrySyncFailures | integration | Correctness | sync errors rate | >0 for 15m | Sev2 | Ticket | Yes | Med | Some customers intentionally block registry egress; clarify in docs. Provide action: check creds, network, certs. | private-day2:model-registry |
| S1 | KubeNodeNotReady | infra | Cluster health | node not ready | >=1 node NotReady for 10m | Sev2 | Ticket | No | High | Too generic (cluster-level). Customers already have this. Don’t ship in Redwood pack. | (omit) |

Notes / deltas vs PRs
- Aligning with observability-pack PR-18356 and PR-18372, but recommending:
  - Gate p99 burn alerts on minimum request volume (to reduce low-traffic spikes).
  - Downgrade GPU util/mem alerts to ticket-level by default; keep OOM + crashloop as paging.
  - Keep client-driven 4xx as dashboard-only.
  - Exclude generic Kubernetes/node alerts from minimum pack.

Recommended changes before GA
1) Add explicit runbook links in alert annotations
- Oncall feedback: alerts should include “What to do first” and a stable runbook URL/anchor.
- Owners: Tomáš Novák (template), Sergio Costa (rule annotations).

2) Add “pairing” guidance to reduce pages that are not actionable
- GPU saturation should not page alone.
- Queue depth should page only when sustained AND either latency burn OR error rate elevated.
- Proposal: encode in expr where possible, otherwise in annotations + default routing to ticket.

3) Adopt consistent grouping labels for Private
- Must have: cluster_id (or customer_cluster), namespace, component, severity.
- Avoid: model, route_id, tenant_id as labels in alerts (cardinality). If needed, include in annotations after hashing/coarsening.
- Owners: Allison Grant (standards), Thomas Baird (cardinality review).

4) Default silences / inhibition rules (strongly suggested for customer Alertmanager)
- Inhibit service-level alerts when Prometheus scrape is failing for that same job (avoid “everything is down” noise).
- Inhibit latency alerts when request volume is below threshold.
- Provide example Alertmanager config snippet in docs.

Customer-facing / Support guidance (what we tell customers)
- Paging expectations: Redwood does not automatically receive pages from customer Alertmanager; these alerts are for customer ops teams. Redwood Support uses them for diagnosis and “what to check” flows.
- Recommended action mapping:
  - Page your on-call: A1/A2/A4/R4/R5/R6/C1/O2
  - Ticket / next-business-day: A3/R7/R8/O1/C2/M1
  - Dashboard-only: A5 (and any optional “baseline drift” alerts)

Open questions
- Should we ship multiwindow burn rate alerts as default, or single-window with simpler semantics?
  - Current recommendation: keep multiwindow for A1/A2; ship simplified single-window equivalents as optional examples.
- Do we require customers to set explicit SLO targets at install time?
  - Recommendation: provide defaults + allow override in values; document that latency SLO depends on model class.

Change log (high level)
- 2025-06-06: Initial pass based on draft alert list and staging burn-in.
- 2025-07-11: Updated based on alert noise review in staging and SUP-49238 (CPU/mem thresholds too tight).
- 2025-08-19: Added gating recommendation for p99 burn + moved GPU util/mem to ticket-level by default.
